report:
Fresh followup assessment of meta.book.index_groups. Before resetting validation I saved/read the previous complete report and inputs. Compared fresh captures with every previous fragment, including recaptured JavaScript and Fixture/chapters helpers. Claim, ordinary test, TODO test, JavaScript and helpers are unchanged. anchors.rs changed only by evidence_status/placeholder_status association comments on page(); spec_plan.rs changed only by the unrelated explicit envelope-clause ownership prerequisite comment. There is no grouping, counting, interaction or test behavior delta.

Full claim assessment: the index must form hierarchical name-prefix groups, allow descendant visibility control, provide separate implementation/test subtree status counts, and use the same active anchor set for groups/counts/rows. The ordinary table implementation obtains names from SpecIndex anchor keys, filters using equality or a dot-delimited prefix, emits each proper prefix once, and selects members from that same names list. Thus sibling string prefixes do not leak and namespace-only groups do not invent anchor rows. Each group has a toggle and independently calculated implementation/test count cells. counts iterates names and the set of statuses present per anchor, so repeated sites do not inflate one status, while a mixed-status anchor contributes to each applicable status. The captured JavaScript maintains per-index collapsed prefixes and separately expanded text. It hides descendant group/anchor/text rows through dot-delimited matching, supports individual and all-group controls, and updates aria state. An anchor identical to a group name is not its own descendant; retained nested collapse state and text-disclosure state remain intentional. These current implementations support the same interpretation as the prior assessment.

Both implementation entries and both tests were reviewed. The ordinary generated_anchor_pages_join_namespaces_claims_implementations_tests_and_reviews test constructs three canonical anchors across parent/child/sibling branches and ordinary/TODO/N/A associations. Assertions require meta and meta.foo group markup, three anchors, visible status counts, exact overview/scoped row membership, sibling isolation, a rule which also owns a namespace, and exactly three canonical definitions after generation. Fixture runs the actual preprocess executable against a temporary workspace; chapters recursively collects paths and rejects duplicates. Assertions are meaningful for generated grouping, membership and basic counts, but the substring count checks do not independently prove every group/column count, and this Rust test does not execute browser interaction.

The associated TODO implementation region and todo::anchor_index_prefix_groups test explicitly retain exhaustive subtree expand/collapse and count verification. The empty body is not proof. Completion requires a DOM/browser fixture with nested/sibling groups, independent implementation/test status combinations, per-group expected counts, and visibility transitions including text rows. This remains a justified visible coverage deferral, not a claim that interaction tests now exist. No N/A entries exist.

The actual marker/comment-only changes do not affect any claim obligation, and all other relied-on captures were verified unchanged. No source changes or test executions occurred in this review; central suites are separately reported. This is a complete current source assessment with preserved limitations, not a blind refresh. No requested edits.
